name: BSWF World Championship
epitaph: The fed's own "Super September" Pay Per View, a six-man tournament, is the fullest surviving account of a title change: Ceesalo defeated Nick Hart in the tournament final to become champion. The Clark held the belt next — his own winning of it is unrecorded, but he defended it into the fed's own Monday Mayhem broadcast, where Wrestletech's interference turned the match and Merchandi$e became champion. Merchandi$e still held the belt as of the fed's own undated Rankings page and its own Thursday Night Thump-Fest broadcast, where Debo carried off the physical belt in a post-match angle without a title actually changing hands — the last-attested state of the championship in the held record.

name: BSWF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The fed's own undated Rankings page names the Made Men (Merchandi$e and Mi$ta) as champions, with Nick Hart and Debo as the #1 contenders — how or when the Made Men won the belts is not recorded. The fed's own Thursday Night Thump-Fest broadcast stages their own only surviving defense, against Kadafi and Scarface, but the referee is pulled from the match before any decision and the text never rules a winner.

name: BSWF Solar Championship
epitaph: Listed vacant on the fed's own undated Rankings page, with no ranked contenders and no champion ever named anywhere in the held record.
notes: No reign is registered — the surviving record never names a Solar Champion.

name: BSWF Lunar Championship
epitaph: Named only as a rankings category on the fed's own undated Rankings page, which gives it no champion, no contenders, and not even the "Vacant" label its Solar counterpart carries.
notes: No reign is registered — the surviving record never names a Lunar Champion.
